head: claude/place-protective-docstring
title: docs(ib): place_protective CANCELS before it places — say so in the docstring
body:
**Tier-1. One docstring. No executable lines change.**

## The defect is the prose, not the code

`IBClient.place_protective`'s docstring said it *"places only the reverse-side protective legs"*. It **also pre-cancels**, and the omission had a measured cost: a session read that docstring, stopped there, and concluded that **no safe in-place repair of a resting protective leg existed**. That is the opposite of the truth, and it is what sent a Tier-3 question to the operator.

*Field beats comment* — the pre-cancel lives in `_locked_place_protective` and is load-bearing (`BL-20260624-MHG-FLIP`: without it, repeated re-arms across an orphan flap stack multiple live OCA brackets on one position, whose stops later fire together and flip a by-then-flat position into a reverse orphan).

## What the docstring now says

Each verified against the body, not inferred:

| claim | where in the body |
|---|---|
| it **cancels before it places** | the pre-cancel block precedes `_build_contract` and every leg placement |
| `oca_key` present -> cancels only `oca-protect-t<key>` | `_cancel_oca_group_for_symbol` |
| `oca_key` absent -> **symbol-wide** cancel that can destroy a sibling's protection on a netted contract (`BL-20260814-IB-PROTECTION-BOOLEAN-NOT-QUANTITY`) | `_cancel_resting_orders_for_symbol`, plus the existing `logger.warning` |
| a pre-cancel that raises is **logged and swallowed**, bracket still armed -- so a success return is **not** proof no stale leg survives | `except Exception ... "proceeding to arm fresh bracket"` |
| `ocaType=1` cancels siblings **within that group only** | the OCA-group comment; this is the disjoint-group hazard behind over-cover-then-naked |
| at least one of `sl`/`tp` required, so an **SL-only caller silently replaces an SL+TP pair with a stop alone** | the `no protective levels` refusal + `legs` assembly |

That last line is stated as **mechanism**, deliberately -- not as a finding about any particular stripped take-profit. `BL-20260816-COVERAGE-IS-ONE-SIDED` records the SL-only-caller theory as an explicitly **unconfirmed** hypothesis for the observed strips, and this PR does not upgrade it.

## Verification

- File parses; docstring attached, 53 lines.
- `pytest -k "place_protective or ib_client or protective"` -> **32 passed**.
- The 98 collection errors and 5 `test_pairs_*` failures in that run are **pre-existing sandbox breakage** (`pyo3_runtime.PanicException`), confirmed **byte-identical on clean `main` with the change stashed** -- checked rather than assumed, since attributing them to this change would have been the comfortable wrong answer. A docstring cannot affect them regardless; CI is the real check.

## Scope

No `src/` executable change, no `config/`, no unit file, no order path, no VM mutation. **No take-profit is attached and no protective leg is repaired** -- the operator declined the attach on 2026-08-20, and the Tier-3 price-reconciler proposal remains draft in #10081.

## Note on CI

`pr-opener.yml`'s results commit is pushed by `github-actions[bot]`, and GitHub does not trigger workflows for pushes made with the built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN`. If that commit lands as this branch's head, the PR will show **zero checks -- blocked, not green**. I will push one ordinary commit to arm CI and will not read a zero-check state as passing.
